text:
alicia: quick follow-up from the canary this morning — noticed a spike in p99 for mid-sized tenants when cohorts rebalanced across GPU lanes. not a full outage but consistent 10-30ms regressions. sharing observations and rough ideas
omar: saw it too. looks correlated with cohort boundary crossing + immediate eviction churn. might be headroom mis-estimates?
jun: can you paste the eviction logs you saw? also which cohort key did we use — seq-length bucketing or tenant-id?
alicia: seq-length bucketing + affinity. logs: ``[evict] lease=lane-3 cohort=seq-128-256 reason=overcommit headroom=-0.12 tokens drop=3``. evictions happen in bursts and then range of inflight windows spikes.
rachael: hmm. that suggests hysteresis for cohort cutover is too low. we have static_half_window=8ms in config currently, maybe it needs to scale with token variance.
omar: propose a layered approach: 1) cohort_hysteresis_ms (soft hold before allowing cutover) 2) headroom_tokens per cohort derived from 95th pct seq len 3) eviction_grace for recently-cutover batches so we don't immediately evict.
alicia: +1. also add a short blacklist for lanes that just had a topology change so new arrivals don't thrash the scheduler for N requests.
jun: what about backlog shaping? if a cohort contributes >X% of in-flight tokens, we throttle acceptance into that cohort until it stabilizes. prevents one cohort surge from starving others.
omar: config prototype (example):
```
cohort_policy: {
  hysteresis_ms: 20
  headroom_tokens_percentile: 95
  headroom_min_tokens: 32
  eviction_grace_ms: 100
  backlog_share_limit: 0.4
}
```
rachael: i worry about increasing hysteresis too much -> added latency for legitimate load shifts. need a fast-path override for explicit canary/pinned requests.
alicia: agreed — add a flag `force_route` for control-plane pinned traffic. not exposed to users by default.
jun: can we compute hysteresis adaptively? e.g., hysteresis_ms = base + alpha * moving_stddev(seq_len) so bursty workloads get longer hold.
omar: yes, adaptive sounds good. also track metrics to make rollback decisions: cohort_cutovers/sec, cutover_latency_ms, eviction_rate, headroom_utilization, p50/p95/p99 latency per-cohort.
ci-bot: deploy pipeline: canary config patch applied to lane-3 at 1723460100 — monitor windows
rachael: experiment plan: A/B lanes — lane-A keep current config, lane-B apply hysteresis/adaptive headroom. run 4-hour runs across peak traffic and compare p99 & tail allocations.
alicia: rollout steps: 1) add telemetry (cutover metrics) 2) conservative defaults (hysteresis 15ms, eviction_grace 80ms) 3) canary on staging lane 3 4) AB test in prod with small % traffic 5) promote if p99 improves or matches and eviction_rate drops by >20%
omar: also add unit tests for ledger accounting so headroom underflow doesn't allow negative tokens. seen subtle bugs there in past.
jun: open questions: - should cohort key include tenant affinity to reduce mixing? - how do we surface when a tenant causes repeated cutovers? (alerts + automatic fallback to dedicated queue?)
alicia: action items: omar to draft config RFC update, jun to add telemetry + tests, rachael to run AB experiment template, i'll coordinate canary window. i'll post the RFC diff by EOD.
omar: thanks. one more: document the invariants we expect from hysteresis (no cutover within Xms unless forced) and add a debug endpoint to force reassign for repro.
rachael: noted. will add to runbook and add a Grafana dashboard panel for cohort churn.
alicia: awesome — thanks team. if anyone sees a regression after canary at 1723460100 ping me or @oncall immediately :thumbsup:
